https://www.dw.com/en/russian-serviceman.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5JTaa The blast killed a man and injured his wife Image: REUTERS Advertisement A lieutenant colonel was killed in a car explosion in Russia's second-largest city, St. Petersburg , on Thursday. Russia's Investigative Committee said the blast occurred in Pushkinsky on the southern outskirts of the city. Neighborhoods in the area are known to house Russian military personnel. Local media suggest the car exploded when the driver turned on the ignition. The victim's wife was also in the car and was rushed to a hospital after the blast. No suspect immediately identified Authorities did not immediately name a suspect, and no group has claimed responsibility. Russia has seen a series of assassinations targeting senior military officials and others linked to the war effort . On August 5, the director of a drone factory was badly wounded and his driver was killed when their car exploded outside the tech hub of Yekaterinburg. Days earlier, on August 1, a bomb at an upscale Italian restaurant in Moscow killed five people, including the bomber. Russia has blamed Ukraine for the attacks. Kyiv has claimed responsibility for some of them while denying involvement in others. Join our team 14 October 2026 The Res Publica Foundation, a Warsaw-based think tank strengthening democratic security and promoting democratic values in Central Europe, is seeking two junior project managers for the Europe Future Forum core team. JUNIOR PROJECT MANAGER We are seeking two full-time colleagues to help implement the full annual project cycle of the Europe Future Forum . Junior project managers will support the presidents of the Foundation in managing our various projects in Poland and across Europe from our office in Warsaw. Their key tasks will relate to the preparation, support and management of the upcoming Europe Future Forum 2027, a strategic community gathering organised annually in Warsaw. A recap of the most recent edition, held in September 2026, is available on the Europe Future Forum website. The main responsibilities will include: Co-organising and co-managing the Europe Future Forum and other international projects of the Foundation Supporting project management, from the application process to final reporting Maintaining contact with project partners and participants, managing the contact database and taking responsibility for the organisation’s customer relationship management system Co-creating the social media strategy and supporting social media outreach Handling other administrative tasks related to the smooth management of projects, as well as reporting to Polish and international authorities and donors Successful candidates will: Required Be responsible, proactive and well-organised team players Be motivated and independent, able to balance different tasks and responsibilities effectively and to collaborate with the Res Publica team Have a command of Polish and English at C1 level or above Be proficient in office software and online tools (Google Workspace and Microsoft Office) Be ready to work from our office in Warsaw Have a problem-solving attitude Desirable Have an interest in policy on democratic security, economic statecraft and European Union (EU) enlargement Have demonstrable knowledge of Central European affairs Have experience in a similar position or in comparable international tasks (international project management) We offer Work as part of an international team Dynamic and creative tasks, including business trips and conferences Contact with senior political and social leaders, experts, academics and representatives of the media and business Influence on the organisation’s agenda Career development that builds on your skills A fully equipped office in the city centre Remuneration of 6,000 Polish zloty To apply, complete the application form by 25 October 2026. Successful candidates should be available to start in November 2026. About us Fundacja Res Publica (the Res Publica Foundation) is a European think tank dedicated to encouraging public debate and raising awareness of democratic values and democratic security in Central Europe. As part of its activities, the Foundation publishes Res Publica Nowa and organises both in-person and online debates. It has also established the Res Publica Think-Tank, a group of distinguished experts specialising in political culture, democracy and public discourse. The Foundation runs Visegrad Insight, an English-language portal and analytical platform based in Warsaw that focuses on European politics, security, geopolitics and the future of democracy. It connects the Central European perspective with broader European and international debates by publishing analyses, commentaries and expert reports. It supports public discourse through collaboration with experts, policymakers and representatives of government, business and academia. A key aspect of its work is strategic foresight, which enables the identification of long-term trends, challenges and development scenarios for Europe. The Europe Future Forum is an international event organised by the Foundation that brings together politicians, public officials, experts, business leaders and representatives of the analytical community to discuss the strategic challenges facing Europe. The Forum provides a platform for in-depth exchanges of views and the development of recommendations on issues such as economic security, EU competitiveness, EU enlargement and democratic resilience. It places particular emphasis on the perspective of Central Europe, including Poland, and on strengthening cooperation between EU member states and candidate countries. The EFF combines public debate with intimate expert sessions and workshops that support relationship-building and the translation of analyses into concrete proposals for action.
